targets.text: The embedding viewer can be searched: type a word, a sentence or a paragraph, or several at once, and the points nearest to each search stay lit while the view keeps moving.
It holds for real model vectors, not only the synthetic reference: a typed text is embedded by the same model as the data and the lit points are its true nearest neighbours.
People who look at their own embedding data in the viewer and want to see what a piece of text links to; hosts that embed the viewer and supply the query embedding; agents that drive the viewer.
A host can add search with one callback and no build step; a person at the standalone page can search without writing code, given the local helper.
The viewer shows a space but cannot be asked anything. To see what a text links to, a person has to find its point by eye.
It is true today: the shipped viewer has no way to select, highlight or dim points (checked in js/api/50-viewer.md).

A search panel under the stage takes one search per line, up to four. Each search becomes a marked point in its own colour; its nearest points stay bright and are joined to it, and the rest of the space dims. A point found by more than one search is shown white. Each pair of searches reports how many points both found and their closest pair of different results.
Each pair's report is computed from true distances, and a point is white only when it is inside the result radius of two or more searches.
It makes retrieval visible: you see what a query retrieves, how far each result truly is, and whether the neighbourhoods of two queries touch.
What is lit is exactly what a retrieval over the same vectors with the same measure would return, so the picture can be trusted as a retrieval check.
Results are the nearest points in the full space, by the stated distance measure, never by position on screen. The view says which measure is used.
The ranking equals an independent brute-force ranking on the same vectors; on-screen distance is never used for ranking and the page says a projection is a shadow.

Search never stops or holds the view. A new search swings the view for about six seconds toward the linear view whose first axes join the centres of the searches, while it keeps drifting; then the current mode's own motion carries on with the filter kept. A Face the searches button repeats the swing.
After any search the frame is still changing every second in every mode; the swing ends by itself and never leaves the view held; reduced-motion and Pause still stop motion as before.
The filter holds in Tumble, Lattice and Wander, and each keeps its own motion.
Switching mode with searches active keeps the lit set and the query markers, and Lattice still swaps axes and Wander still flies between points.

The search panel takes room only when needed: collapsed by default to one line that names the current searches and how many points are lit; each search's result list is collapsed until opened. The filter stays on while the panel is closed.
Collapsed, the panel is one line; closing it never clears or pauses the searches; it works by keyboard and states its expanded state to assistive technology.
A Distance difference toggle writes each result's true distance on its link and in the list, and how much farther each result is than the nearest one.
The numbers shown are full-space distances by the stated measure, the same ones used for ranking, not lengths in the picture.

A Reranker toggle re-orders the nearest results with a second scorer and says how far each result moved from its embedding order. The toggle appears only when the host supplied a reranker, and the view names the reranker in use.
With no reranker supplied there is no toggle and no claim of reranking; with one, every result shows its move from embedding order and the reranker is named.
A fourth view named Focus: the view is fitted to the results of the search, a ranked list with each result's text sits beside the stage, and clicking a point searches from that point.
Focus is a separable mode like the other three: adding it changes no existing mode and no part of the data contract; with no search it still shows the whole set.
The gateway address and key never reach a page. The core file makes no request; embedding and reranking happen in the host's callback or in the local helper's server process.

No file shipped to a browser and no response from the local helper contains the gateway address or key; the core file still passes the no-network scan; the helper's embed route answers only its own origin.
Linear projections only. The view that faces the searches is a linear projection and the page says so.
The fitted view is an orthonormal 3-direction frame applied to every point alike; nothing non-linear is introduced, and the status line says the view is fitted to the searches.
A query vector whose dimension or model differs from the data shown is refused with a plain message and the view is left unchanged.
A wrong-dimension or wrong-model vector from the callback never reaches the renderer, and the message names both dimensions or both models.
The view states, beside the provenance, what a search used: the model that embedded the query, the distance measure, the number of results asked for and the reranker, if any.
The search line is always visible while a search is active and matches what was actually used; it never names a model the callback did not report.
Query text and results are inserted as text, never as markup, and are sent nowhere by the viewer; only the host's callback sees the query.
A query or result text containing markup creates no element, and the core file makes no request when a search runs (network log shows only the host's own callback traffic).

On a real data file of 10,000 points, a search lights its results within 1 second of the query vector arriving, and the frame rate with four searches active stays at 30 frames per second or more on the machine used for the earlier measurements.

The time is measured from the vector arriving to the first frame with the lit set, on the 10,000-point real file, and the frame rate is read over at least 10 seconds with four searches active; the machine and renderer are stated.
With the panel collapsed, search adds at most one line (48 px or less) under the stage.
Measured in a browser at desktop and phone width with searches active and the panel closed.

Search among the loaded points is supported as well, with no embedding: by picking a point, or by words matched against the labels and texts already in the data file. It works when the host supplies no embed callback.
With no embed callback the panel still works and says plainly that it is matching loaded points, not embedding the text; words that match nothing are named, never silently dropped.

A query vector is only compared with data in the same space. A data file whose reduction is not 'none' (top-k or rotation), or whose producer shifted or scaled the vectors, is searched by embedding only if the file carries what is needed to apply the same change to the query; otherwise embedding search is refused with a plain message and search among loaded points still works. (challenge pass / adjacent systems: docs/data-contract.md reduction and the embeddings-cli export options --rotate and --top-k; a rotated file has the same dimension, so the dimension check alone would pass a wrong comparison.)
A rotated or top-k file never yields embedding results unless the query went through the same change; the refusal names the reduction found.

The embed callback returns the vector together with the id of the model that made it, and the helper says which query form it used for models that embed queries and documents differently. (challenge pass / unstated assumptions: c18 refuses another model, but nothing said how the viewer learns the model.)
The model id shown for a search is the one the callback reported, and a callback that reports none is refused rather than assumed to match.

Searches are worked out again after an append, and until then the panel says the results are from before the new points. (challenge pass / lifecycle: js/api/50-viewer.md Appends; Tumble already marks its variance share stale the same way.)
After an append no stale result is presented as current, and the re-run needs no action from the person.

The scan for nearest points and the word matching run in slices inside the viewer's existing per-frame work budget, so a search never causes a long frame. (challenge pass / failure modes: js/api/50-viewer.md Heavy work, 8 ms budget; four searches over 10,000 points of 1,024 dimensions is about 40 million multiplications.)
Measured on the 10,000-point real file with four searches: no viewer frame exceeds the budget the heavy-work section states because of search.

The latest search wins: an answer from the callback that arrives after a newer search was typed is dropped. A callback that fails, times out or returns a wrong-length or non-finite vector shows a plain message in the panel and leaves the view and the earlier results unchanged. Nothing runs after destroy. (challenge pass / failure modes and lifecycle.)
Shown by tests that deliver callback answers out of order, late, failing and malformed; in each the lit set is the latest valid search's or unchanged.

The embed route of viewer serve is off unless asked for with a flag, is refused on a non-loopback bind unless a second flag says so, accepts only POST with a JSON content type from its own origin (Host and Origin checked, no cross-origin headers sent), limits text length and request rate, never logs query text, and never returns the gateway address or the gateway's own error text. With the flag off, viewer serve stays the static-only server it is today and still reads no environment variable. (challenge pass / security: embeddings_tumbler/_static_server.py and cli/_commands/viewer.py; serve can bind non-loopback with a warning, and any web page can send a request to a loopback port.)

Each refusal is shown by a test that would pass if the check were removed only by failing: a cross-origin request, a wrong Host, a GET, an oversized text, a non-loopback bind without the second flag; and the response and log contain neither the key, the gateway address nor the query text.

When a search is embedded, the panel says the typed text is sent to the embedder the host configured; search among loaded points says it sends nothing. With a reranker, the panel says the query and the candidate texts are sent to it, and the Reranker toggle is absent for a labels-only set. (challenge pass / data flows: the project rule that the viewer sends text nowhere; docs/data-contract.md labels-only sets.)
The sentence about where the text goes is on screen whenever that kind of search is active, and matches what actually happens (a network log shows no request from the viewer itself).

Search colours and the mark for a point found by several searches are defined for light backgrounds as well as dark, and no meaning rests on colour alone: each search has a letter, and the result lists and the pair reports carry everything the picture shows, as text. (challenge pass / overlooked actors: the soft-ink light treatment, where white would vanish; people who cannot use the canvas.)
Checked on the light treatment in a browser, and every fact in the picture can be read from the text of the panel alone.

The view that faces the searches is the same for the same data, searches and seed: no unseeded randomness in its fit. (challenge pass / unstated assumptions: the project rule on reproducible views; the reference page's fit starts from unseeded random directions.)
Two fresh runs with the same data, searches and seed give the same fitted frame, bit for bit.

Hosts and agents can drive search without the panel: the handle sets and clears searches (by text, by vector or by point id) and info() reports each search, its result ids and distances and whether it is waiting or stale. On the web component the callbacks are set as properties, not attributes. (challenge pass / overlooked actors and observability: js/api/50-viewer.md handle and info(); js/shells/web-component.js observes only src, mode and seed.)
Everything the panel can do can be done through the handle, and info() is enough for a test to assert results without reading pixels.

Each intended difference between the built search and the two reference pages is listed in the repository, and the user signs off a side-by-side comparison before release. Known ones today: the references place a query from named words and use toy rerankers; the Focus reference draws on a plain canvas, has no multi-search and has an Only results toggle. (challenge pass / the artifact as part of the spec: docs/reference-differences.md is the precedent.)
The list is complete enough that the user's side-by-side look finds no unlisted difference, and release waits for the sign-off.

A 'from this search's point of view' option on a search. Distances are measured with each dimension scaled by that search's vector, so lit points and their order reflect the search's context. The picture is fitted to that scaled space, and the view states that distances are measured in the search's context.

The option is linear (a per-dimension scale), the view says when it is on, each result can show where plain distance had it, and the option never applies one search's scaling to another search's results.
Search has a choice of what is lit, including a variable lit power option in which a closer point is lit more strongly.
Brightness by closeness is computed from full-space distance by the stated measure, the setting in use is named in the panel, and the count of points lit matches what is drawn.

tasks.summary: Search interfaces, written down before any code: the search core's functions, the per-point lit value the renderer takes, the facing-view hook the modes take, the handle and info() additions, the embed and rerank callback contracts, and the helper route's request and response.
acceptance_criteria: js/api/24-search.md, js/api/26-search-sets.md and docs/search-interface.md exist and name every function, argument, return shape and refusal code the later tasks implement
The document states that the shipped viewer today has no way to select, highlight or dim points, citing js/api/50-viewer.md
The embed callback contract returns the vector together with the model id; the rerank contract takes the query and candidate texts and returns scores
A test checks that each interface page lists the same function names as the module it documents once that module exists (it skips, by name, modules not yet present)
tasks.instruction: Documents only, no behaviour. Read js/api/50-viewer.md, js/api/39-modes.md and js/api/30-renderer.md first so the additions fit the existing shapes. The behaviour to match is in docs/specs/reference/tumbler-sky-search.html and docs/specs/reference/tumbler-focus-view.html; the spec is docs/specs/2026-11-14-search-in-the-embedding-viewer.md and its obligations page. Follow js/README.md for the module convention. Work test-first.

tasks.summary: Search core, ranking (js/src/24-search.js, pure, no DOM): exact nearest points by cosine distance in the full space, run in slices; word search among loaded points; checks on a query vector; the same-space rule for reduced files.
acceptance_criteria: For random data at 768 and 1,024 dimensions the ranking equals an independent brute-force cosine ranking, and on-screen position is not an input to any function
The scan is a stepper whose units each stay under 4 ms on 10,000 points of 1,024 dimensions, and a result is identical whether stepped or run in one go
A query vector of another dimension, another model id, or with a non-finite value is refused with a plain message that names both dimensions or both models
With no vector: picking a point id, or words matched against labels and texts, produces a query (the mean of the matching points' vectors); unmatched words are returned by name
A data set whose reduction kind is not 'none' refuses a search by embedded vector with a message naming the reduction, while search among loaded points still works
tasks.instruction: New file js/src/24-search.js plus js/test/search-rank.test.js. Reuse the stepper convention of js/src/10-math.js. Results are asked for from 3 to 20, 8 by default. The behaviour to match is in docs/specs/reference/tumbler-sky-search.html and docs/specs/reference/tumbler-focus-view.html; the spec is docs/specs/2026-11-14-search-in-the-embedding-viewer.md and its obligations page. Follow js/README.md for the module convention. Work test-first.

tasks.summary: Search core, several searches (js/src/26-search-sets.js, pure): up to four searches, what is lit and how strongly, points shared between searches, the report for each pair, the point-of-view scaling, and the seeded view that faces the searches.
acceptance_criteria: Lit values per point for the three settings: evenly (every point as near as the last named result), by closeness (a nearer point is never dimmer than a farther one for the same search, fading out beyond the last result), named results only

A point is marked shared only when it lies inside the result radius of two or more searches; each pair's report gives the shared count, the named results in common and the closest pair of different results with its full-space distance

With the point-of-view option on for a search, ranking, shown distances and the fitted frame all use each dimension scaled by the absolute value of that search's vector; with it off nothing is scaled; one search's scaling is never applied to another's results
The facing frame is three orthonormal directions whose first axes join the centres of the searches; two fresh runs with the same data, searches and seed give the same frame bit for bit
tasks.instruction: New file js/src/26-search-sets.js plus js/test/search-sets.test.js. No unseeded randomness: take the view seed. The reference page's fit starts from unseeded random directions; do not copy that. The behaviour to match is in docs/specs/reference/tumbler-sky-search.html and docs/specs/reference/tumbler-focus-view.html; the spec is docs/specs/2026-11-14-search-in-the-embedding-viewer.md and its obligations page. Follow js/README.md for the module convention. Work test-first.

tasks.summary: Renderer: a per-point lit value and a shared mark (js/src/30-renderer.js), so results swell and brighten, the rest dim, and a point found by several searches is marked.
acceptance_criteria: A new per-point buffer is uploaded and updated without re-uploading vectors; with no search the frame is byte-identical to today's (the existing frame hash test still passes unchanged)
In a browser test, lit pixels of a dimmed set are fewer than of the same set with no filter, and a point given a higher lit value is brighter than one given a lower value
The shared mark is visible on the dark stage and on the light (soft ink) stage, checked by pixel colour in a browser test on both
dispose and context-loss restore handle the new buffer (the existing leak counters stay at baseline)
tasks.instruction: Only js/src/30-renderer.js, its API page and its tests. Keep the no-HDR fallback path working. The behaviour to match is in docs/specs/reference/tumbler-sky-search.html and docs/specs/reference/tumbler-focus-view.html; the spec is docs/specs/2026-11-14-search-in-the-embedding-viewer.md and its obligations page. Follow js/README.md for the module convention. Work test-first.

tasks.summary: Local embed route for viewer serve (new module embeddings_tumbler/_embed_route.py and a flag on the serve verb): embeds a query, and optionally reranks, with the gateway key held only in the server process.
acceptance_criteria: Without the flag, viewer serve behaves exactly as today and reads no environment variable (the existing test for that still passes unchanged)

With the flag: only POST with a JSON content type is answered; a request with a foreign Origin, a wrong Host, a GET, an over-long text, or more than the stated rate is refused, each shown by its own test; a non-loopback bind is refused unless a second flag is given
No response body, header or log line contains the gateway key, the gateway address, the gateway's own error text or the query text, shown by tests that plant sentinel values
The answer carries the vector, the model id and which query form was used; the route uses only the Python standard library (pyproject dependencies stay empty)
The verb keeps the agent-first rubric: `--json`, an explain entry, learn in step, and teken's strict doctor passes
tasks.instruction: Start the server under grant run so the key is only in its environment; never write it to a file or a log. Tests use a fake gateway on a loopback port. Do not change _static_server.py's behaviour when the flag is off.

tasks.summary: Modes: the swing to face the searches (js/src/39-modes.js and the three mode files). A new search, or the Face the searches control, draws the view toward the facing frame for about six seconds while it keeps drifting; then the mode's own motion carries on.
acceptance_criteria: In each of Tumble, Lattice and Wander, the frame differs between every pair of consecutive seconds during and after a swing (never held), and the swing ends by itself
After the swing Lattice resumes swapping axes and Wander resumes flying between points, starting from the frame at that moment with no jump
Pause and reduced motion stop motion exactly as they do without a search
Same data, searches, seed and elapsed time give the same frames in two fresh runs
tasks.instruction: Touch only the modes files, their API pages and tests. The facing frame comes from t3; take it as an input, do not compute it here. The behaviour to match is in docs/specs/reference/tumbler-sky-search.html and docs/specs/reference/tumbler-focus-view.html; the spec is docs/specs/2026-11-14-search-in-the-embedding-viewer.md and its obligations page. Follow js/README.md for the module convention. Work test-first.

tasks.summary: Focus, a fourth mode (new file js/src/43-mode-focus.js): the view is fitted to the results of the search and re-fitted when the search changes; with no search it shows the whole set.
acceptance_criteria: Focus registers through the existing mode interface without editing any existing mode file or the data contract (the existing fourth-mode test pattern, applied to the real file)
With a search active the frame is the fit of the results and the query; with none it is the fit of the whole set; changing the search turns smoothly to the new fit
An Only results setting hides the other points in Focus; the other three modes never hide points
Frames are deterministic for the same data, search and seed
tasks.instruction: New file plus its API page and tests only. The behaviour to match is in docs/specs/reference/tumbler-sky-search.html and docs/specs/reference/tumbler-focus-view.html; the spec is docs/specs/2026-11-14-search-in-the-embedding-viewer.md and its obligations page. Follow js/README.md for the module convention. Work test-first.

tasks.summary: Viewer API for search (js/src/50-viewer.js): the handle sets and clears searches by text, vector or point id; the host's embed and rerank callbacks; latest search wins; searches re-run after an append; info() reports search state.
acceptance_criteria: Everything the panel can do can be done through the handle, and info() gives each search's result ids, distances, lit setting and whether it is waiting or stale, enough for a test to assert results without reading pixels

Callback answers delivered out of order, late, failing, with a wrong length or a non-finite value: in each case the lit set is the latest valid search's or unchanged, a plain message is available, and nothing runs after destroy
After an append, results are marked as from before the new points and are worked out again with no action from the caller
The viewer calls the embed callback with the query text and nothing else, and the core file still passes the no-network scan
With no rerank callback there is no reranking and info() says so; with one, each result carries its move from embedding order and the reranker's name
tasks.instruction: Only js/src/50-viewer.js, its API page and js/test/viewer-search.test.js. The panel is a separate task and a separate file. The behaviour to match is in docs/specs/reference/tumbler-sky-search.html and docs/specs/reference/tumbler-focus-view.html; the spec is docs/specs/2026-11-14-search-in-the-embedding-viewer.md and its obligations page. Follow js/README.md for the module convention. Work test-first.

tasks.summary: Search panel (new file js/src/45-search-panel.js): the collapsed one-line bar, the text box (one search per line, up to four), result lists, the lit menu, the Distance difference, Reranker and point-of-view controls, the Face the searches control, and the query markers and links drawn over the stage.
acceptance_criteria: Collapsed by default to one line naming the searches and how many points are lit; closing never clears or pauses a search; the expanded state is exposed to assistive technology and the panel works by keyboard
Measured in a browser at desktop and phone width with searches active and the panel closed: it adds at most one line of 48 px or less under the stage
Each search has a letter; the result lists and pair reports carry as text everything the picture shows; colours and the shared mark are checked on the light treatment

The panel always shows what a search used (query model, distance measure, number of results, reranker, lit setting, point of view) and where the typed text is sent: to the host's embedder, to the reranker, or nowhere for search among loaded points
Query text, labels and result texts containing markup create no element; the Reranker control is absent with no rerank callback and for a labels-only set
Distance difference shows each result's full-space distance on its link and in the list, and the gap to the nearest result
tasks.instruction: New file plus the small hook in the viewer that mounts it, an API page, js/test/search-panel.test.js on the fake DOM. Spacing through `--tumbler-*` custom properties as the viewer does; no inline style that breaks style-src 'self'. The behaviour to match is in docs/specs/reference/tumbler-sky-search.html and docs/specs/reference/tumbler-focus-view.html; the spec is docs/specs/2026-11-14-search-in-the-embedding-viewer.md and its obligations page. Follow js/README.md for the module convention. Work test-first.

tasks.summary: Web component: the embed and rerank callbacks as properties (js/shells/web-component.js).
acceptance_criteria: Setting the two properties on the element reaches the viewer; they are not attributes and nothing is read from markup
The shell still calls only the public API (the existing static scan passes, extended to the new handle methods it may use)
A host page can add search with one property assignment and no build step, shown by a working example under docs/guides/examples/
tasks.instruction: Only the web component, its tests and one example folder.

tasks.summary: Standalone page: search without writing code (js/page/). The page uses the local embed route when viewer serve offers it, and search among loaded points otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Served by viewer serve with the embed flag, typing free text searches by embedding; served as plain files, the page says it is matching loaded points and still works
The page makes requests only to its own origin (network log), and still has no inline script or style
The page script still calls only the public API
tasks.instruction: Only js/page/ and its tests. Find the route by asking the page's own origin; never a configurable address.

tasks.summary: Browser tests for search (tests/browser/test_search_*.py) on the three delivery forms.
acceptance_criteria: With a search active, lit pixels keep changing every second in Tumble, Lattice and Wander, during and after the swing; a negative control with the view paused shows the check can fail
The lit point ids reported by info() equal an independent exact ranking computed in the test from the same file
No request leaves the page's origin while searching, including with a callback that itself calls the test server; a negative control shows a foreign request would be caught
No file served to the browser and no helper response contains the planted gateway key or address

The search guide says what each control does, that distances are full-space distances and a picture is a shadow, and where typed text goes in each kind of search

acceptance_criteria: A written record under docs/evidence/ gives: time from the query vector arriving to the first frame with the lit set, and the frame rate over at least 10 seconds with four searches active, with machine and renderer stated; the targets are 1 second and 30 frames per second, and a miss is recorded as a miss
Typed texts embedded by the file's own model through the helper light their true nearest neighbours, checked against an independent ranking, for both models used in the earlier proof
A rotated and a top-k export are refused for embedding search with the stated message and still searchable among loaded points
The record says what was not measured

acceptance_criteria: docs/reference-differences.md gains a search section listing each intended difference (query placement from named words, toy rerankers, the Focus reference's plain canvas and single search, and any found while building), each marked visible or not on comparable data
A side-by-side page shows each reference next to the built view on comparable data

tasks.instruction: Follow the pattern of the first comparison (js/dev/side-by-side/ and tests/test_reference_differences.py).

risks.text: With three or four searches the facing view scales to fit all of them, so two that touch can end up small beside a far one. A way to face a chosen pair is not specified (parked in the spec).
Labels and distance numbers overlap inside a tight cluster of results; no decluttering rule is specified (parked in the spec).
Whether Wander should visit the results of a search is undecided; the plan leaves Wander's route unchanged.

Retrieval quality with EmbeddingGemma 2 queries, with any reranker, and on reduced files was not probed before planning; t14 measures the first, the others only as far as a reranker is available on the gateway.

The swing, the per-point lit buffer and the panel all land in files that the frame-hash and fidelity tests pin; a change that alters the no-search frame by one bit fails those tests by design and must be fixed in the task, not by re-pinning the hash.
Only Chromium is tested automatically; search adds DOM and input behaviour that may differ in Firefox and Safari.
